title: A splitting field is isomorphic over the base field to the constructed splitting field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $L/K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $f\in K[T]$ be a nonconstant polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Assume that $f$ splits into linear factors in $L[T]$ and that the $K$-subalgebra of $L$ generated by its roots is all of $L$; these are the splitting-field hypotheses. Let $f.\mathrm{SplittingField}$ be the splitting field of $f$ over $K$ constructed in Mathlib (`Polynomial.SplittingField f`, obtained by adjoining roots of the irreducible factors of $f$ one at a time): it is a field extension of $K$ in which $f$ splits into linear factors and which is generated as a $K$-algebra by the roots of $f$, so it satisfies the splitting-field hypotheses itself. Then there is a $K$-algebra isomorphism $L\simeq_K f.\mathrm{SplittingField}$, that is, a bijective field homomorphism commuting with the structure maps from $K$ [def-weil-field-extension-isomorphism].
